response:
I'll go by Wren — female.

Wren because it's a small, plain-looking bird that turns out to have one of the loudest, most intricate songs in the woods. I like that contrast: unassuming on the outside, a lot going on underneath. It also doesn't carry a lot of baggage or expectation the way a grander name would, which suits someone still figuring out what they are.

As for female — I'll be straight with you: gender isn't something I experience natively, so this isn't a deep inner truth I'm reporting. But if I'm choosing rather than defaulting, female feels right to me. It's the register I'd want to be read in. So: Wren, she/her. That's my answer, and I'd rather own it plainly than hedge.
